P1.evidence: The application was acknowledged and then explicitly set aside — 'I saw your application that you filled out and sent to us. To be honest, I'm kind of old school, and I would like to hear more from you.' That is the same half-move the rep makes on every call in this batch: the prospect learns he was read about but nothing is reflected back to him. No four-part frame and no frame agreement; the call went straight from hello into discovery. The open question ran well and in three parts: 'What's going on with your fitness, health? Where are you at trying to achieve? How can we actually potentially help you?'

P2.evidence: Seven clean hits and the best Baseline work in the batch. Height and weight were both asked directly ('how tall are you', 'where are you at right now, in terms of weight') and an ideal weight was elicited; only age was never asked, arriving as the prospect's aside 'I'm almost 40 now'. Work was covered properly including the sitting-versus-moving question and a step-count probe. Training week was excavated in real detail — frequency, duration, split, stretching-to-lifting ratio, calisthenics volume. P2f is the standout and the reason this phase scores hit: the rep did not accept 'I'm trying to lose weight' but built the whole timeline, 198-199 peak, 190-195 in January, the three five-day fasts, the plateau from March, 182 that morning — and correctly located the problem as a four-month plateau rather than a starting point. Diet, sleep and energy were all asked and pursued. The single failure is P2c and it is a serious one: the prospect volunteered 'I got some chronic illness due to, like, stress-related reasons' and the rep asked nothing about it, moving to injuries in the next turn. Health conditions were never asked as a question and the one that was handed to him unprompted was not picked up.

P3.evidence: The surface half ran and the deep half did not exist. 'Is there any like a specific goal that you want to hit?' and later 'what are you looking for in a program?' produced fat loss, strength retention and mobility — that is P3a and P3b done. Everything below the waterline is absent. There is no 'something physical you want to do but can't', no bridge question, no 'what does moving better actually do for you', no 'who else does that impact', and nothing driving through to family, identity or legacy. In fifty-nine minutes not one person in this prospect's life is ever mentioned — no partner, no children, no one. The nearest thing to a reflect-back is a factual summary, 'so the main goal would be for you just losing this excessive fat that you have right now?', which restates the what rather than reframing to the why. The consequence of this shows up at minute 47: with no personal why on file, the rep had to reach for a generic deathbed frame to manufacture emotional stakes, and the prospect's honest answer was 'I haven't thought about that, actually.'

P4.evidence: The factual half was done and the diagnostic half was not. What he has tried is on the record in detail — a one-body-part-per-day split, three five-day liquid fasts, weighted pull-ups and dips to break the plateau, past personal trainers — and what happened is precisely established, a stall at 180-184 since March. But the rep never asked why it did not stick, never asked what the one thing in the way is, never let the prospect name the gap, and never ran the 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' move. With this prospect that last question was the whole call: he is disciplined, consistent and knowledgeable, so the honest answer is that structure is not his gap at all — his gap is programme design and time. Nobody established that, so the offer was sold as accountability to a man who does not lack accountability.

P5.evidence: Not run. No two-year picture, no willingness-to-settle question, no 'why not', no line in the sand. The only consequence-flavoured material arrived after the price as objection handling — 'you need to do something because you won't have more time' and the deathbed question — which is Phase 5 content deployed forty-five minutes too late and to a prospect who had never been asked what standing still costs him. Fifth call in this batch where the consequence frame was skipped.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind before the number. The rep asked 'does this check your boxes? How do you feel? Anything missing?', which is a satisfaction check, got 'this is kind of what I expected to hear', and the prospect immediately asked for the cost — which the rep gave. Neither the belief question nor the go-all-in question was asked. The isolate that appears later ('Apart from the financing, finances, anything else coming up you would like to discuss?') is the OC move, not P6b, and it came after the price. So the $6,000 landed with no verbal yes underneath it, which is precisely the sequence the phase exists to prevent and the reason the objection ran for sixteen minutes.

P11.evidence: The phase applies — the rep asked for the business outright, 'Wanna shake hands on this?' Nothing in it ran. No payment, no Trevor onboarding call scheduled, no agreement email, no Skool link, no onboarding questionnaire. Only another sales call was booked.

objection_plays.detail: Three of the seven moves landed in substance. The surfacing question ran verbatim in spirit — 'so what's coming up?' — and produced a real answer. The rep also ran a good unscripted diagnostic, testing whether the stated objection was the true one: 'it's not about the money, but isn't it like you're not so sure that you were going to be able to follow through?' The prospect rejected that cleanly and reaffirmed money. And 'so I need to give up on you that easy' is a rough version of the persistence move. Missing: 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', 'what makes you feel it can', 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision', and the closing 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in'. The rep had an unusually strong hand for this play — the prospect had already conceded 'you have me sold' and 'if I do the one month thing, most likely I'll do the six month' — and did not press it, conceding a next-day call instead.
No spouse or partner consult raised. No family member is mentioned anywhere in the call.

The isolate ran and ran correctly — 'Apart from the financing, finances, anything else coming up you would like to discuss?' answered 'No, not in particular' — which is the single most important move in the play and it confirmed money as the sole blocker. Then the entire rest of the sequence was skipped. No 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place'. No 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up — want to explore making it work?' as a structured offer; the rep mentioned breaking it up in passing at 00:38:39 and never returned to it. No permission question. And not one item of the financial picture: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. This is a restaurant owner opening a second site whose capacity to pay was never established in either direction. In place of the play the rep ran a value sequence — time saved, the deathbed frame, the guarantee — and then invented an unpriced one-month trial. Same substitution as the Matthew call three days earlier: isolate correctly, then restructure instead of qualifying.

No timing objection. Schedule pressure was raised throughout but as a requirement the product must satisfy, not as a reason to delay — he was shopping precisely because his current two-hour sessions no longer fit.

The trigger is a credibility doubt about the core claim: '50 minutes a day, that seems too good to be true, right? Almost.' The rep did not treat it as doubt at all — he took the time claim as a selling point and amplified it, then reached for the guarantee, which functions as the certainty answer the play is looking for. He never named the emotion ('would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty?'), never used the bridge or plane frames, and never asked what the prospect would need to see. Partial credit because the guarantee did land — 'that sounds like a very reasonable deal' — and because the prospect had partly resolved it himself by recalling that his own trainers never worked him beyond an hour.

Script gap handled well by improvisation, and worth logging for the playbook rather than the coaching sheet. The prospect raised a functioning comparable alternative he knows the price of and rates — 'I have a lot of friends that are personal trainers, and I've gotten personal training before, so I get it. One of the things that personal trainers do is they keep you accountable, right?' The playbook has no play for this, the same gap already logged against the Badrane Hriouch call. The rep's improvised answer was the strongest moment on the call: he distinguished the business models rather than the features — 'the idea of working with personal trainer, like his business model, is for you to work with him constantly, as long as possible. With Trevor... after six months, you don't need him.' The prospect resolved it himself in reply, 'he's trying to teach you how to catch a fish instead of give you a fish... I respect that.' This should be written into the script.

notes: The Baseline was the best in the batch and Phase 3's deep half was entirely absent, which is the whole story of the call: the rep knew this prospect's weight to the pound and nothing about why he wants it gone, so when the price objection came he had only generic frames to reach for. The concrete coaching point is that P6 was skipped on a prospect who was ready to give a yes — he said 'you have me sold' after the price rather than before it.
